To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

2-[I-125]iodomelatonin binding sites in hamsters are specific for the indoleamine, are saturable, reversible, and of high affinity, and are found in the highest concentrations in the pineal gland and in lower concentrations in other areas of the brain.
2-[I-125]iodomelatonin binds to high affinity sites in Syrian hamster brain with an affinity constant of 3.2 +/- 0.6 nM and a binding capacity of 110.1 +/- 13.5 fmol/mg membrane protein.
2-[I-125]iodomelatonin is a selective radioligand for identifying high affinity melatonin binding sites in rodents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of radioligands for the study of melatonin receptors.
the identification of the site(s) of action of melatonin in the hamster.
the identification of the mechanism by which melatonin mediates its photoperiodic effect on reproduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

2-[I-125]iodomelationin is a high affinity and selective ligand for the melatonin receptor in hamster brain and that this receptor is present in the hypothalamus, pineal gland, and other areas of the brain.
the binding site is not a serotonin receptor but rather a receptor for melatonin.
2-[I-125]iodomelatonin is a selective and potent ligand for melatonin receptors in hamster brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 125I-labeled indole is a selective and high affinity ligand for melatonin receptors and that these sites are widely distributed in hamster brain.
melatonin binding sites in the hamster brain are highly selective for indoles.
the 2-[125]iodomelatone binding sites in hamsters brain membranes are selective and specific to the indoleamine melatonin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
2-iodo- N -acetyl melatonin is a selective ligand for melatonin receptors and that melatonin receptors are expressed in the hamster brain.
2-[I-125]iodomelatonin is a selective high affinity radioligand for melatonin binding sites in rodential brain.
the melatonin receptors are a class of receptors that are distinct from the serotonergic, dopaminergic, adrengeric, and histaminergic receptors.
